newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair invites offers for 12 new aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Finnair invites offers for 12 new aircraft.

text.p: Finnish national airline Finnair Oy said in a statement on Friday it had decided to ask European Airbus Industrie and U.S. Boeing Co for offers for 12 new aircraft to replace its ageing DC9s.
"Both manufacturers have a family of aircraft representing three different sizes and suitable for Finnair's purposes," it said.

Finnair said prices for the aircraft varied according to size between $25 million and $40 million. "The value of the acquisitions now under consideration would be around two billion markka," it said, adding: "Some of the aircraft can be leased." It did not elaborate.
Finnair said it expected to receive the offers during April after which "final comparisons" would start. "No deadline has been set for the decision to order," it said.
"The decision on selection of aircraft sizes will be made when the order is placed," Finnair said.
"Deliveries would be scheduled so that the aircraft could begin service in 1999-2001," it said.

The Airbus planes under consideration -- the A319, A320 and A321 -- can seat between 128 and 188 passengers. The Boeing aircraft -- the B737-600, B737-700 and B-737-800 -- have seats for between 111 and 165 passengers, it said.
The McDonnel Douglas DC9s to be retired have 121 passenger seats, Finnair said. -- Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
